source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: General Awareness
question_text: The modern Olympic Games were revived and first held in 1896 in which city?
explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were organized under the auspices of Pierre de Coubertin in Athens in 1896.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: General Awareness
question_text: The Sun Temple, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984, is located at:
explanation: The 13th-century Sun Temple at Konark was constructed in the shape of a colossal chariot by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error:
'Neither of the two candidates (A) / have submitted (B) / their original documents (C) / on time. (D)'
explanation: 'Neither of' is singular distributive pronoun and takes a singular verb. 'have submitted' must be replaced by 'has submitted'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Find the part with an error:
'She was so tired (A) / that she could not (B) / hardly walk (C) / any further. (D)'
explanation: 'Hardly' itself carries a negative meaning. Using 'could not' with 'hardly' creates an incorrect double negative. It should be 'she could hardly walk'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Identify the error segment:
'The scenery of Kashmir (A) / are more beautiful (B) / than that of Himachal. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb. 'are' should be replaced by 'is'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Find the grammatical error:
'No sooner did he entered (A) / the classroom (B) / than the bell rang. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The auxiliary verb 'did' must be followed by base form of verb (V1). It should be 'did he enter', not 'entered'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Identify the error segment:
'One of my friend (A) / is visiting (B) / me this weekend. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The construction 'one of' is always followed by a plural noun. It must be 'One of my friends'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Find the error:
'Although he worked hard, (A) / but he failed (B) / in the examination. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: 'Although' is paired with 'yet' or a comma, never with 'but'. 'but' should be removed.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Identify the error:
'The teacher asked the students (A) / to not make (B) / any noise in the library. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: Split infinitive: the standard negative infinitive construction is 'not to make', rather than 'to not make'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Find the error segment:
'Ten miles are (A) / a long distance (B) / to walk on foot. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: When a plural noun represents a single collective distance or quantity, it takes a singular verb. 'are' should be 'is'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Identify the error:
'Each of the girls (A) / have done (B) / her homework diligently. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: 'Each' is singular and requires a singular verb. 'have done' must be replaced by 'has done'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Find the error:
'He congratulated me (A) / for my success (B) / in the competitive exam. (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The verb 'congratulate' takes the preposition 'on', not 'for'. It should be 'on my success'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank:
He is completely absorbed ______ his research work.
explanation: The adjective 'absorbed' takes the fixed preposition 'in' when denoting deep mental involvement.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the appropriate word:
The principal ______ the prizes to the winners at the annual sports day.
explanation: Phrasal verb 'give away' means to distribute prizes or gifts publicly.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Fill in the blank:
I have not seen him ______ last Monday.
explanation: 'Since' is used for a specific point in past time with the Present Perfect tense.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the correct preposition:
She insists ______ accompanying her brother to the market.
explanation: The verb 'insist' takes the fixed preposition 'on' followed by a gerund.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Fill in the blank:
Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present in the auditorium.
explanation: With 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('students', plural). Thus 'were' is correct.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the word to fill the blank:
The committee ______ divided in their opinions regarding the proposal.
explanation: When members of a collective noun act individually or disagree, a plural verb ('were') is used.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Fill in the blank:
Hard work is the key ______ success.
explanation: The fixed prepositional phrase is 'key to success'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Choose the correct option:
If I ______ a bird, I would fly to you.
explanation: In subjunctive conditional mood expressing hypothetical or unreal wishes, 'were' is used with all subjects.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Fill in the blank:
He prevented me ______ entering the restricted room.
explanation: The verb 'prevent' governs the preposition 'from' followed by a gerund (-ing).
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the appropriate word:
The firemen managed to ______ the raging fire within two hours.
explanation: The phrasal verb 'put out' means to extinguish a fire.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

question_text: Select the meaning of the idiom: 'Once in a blue moon'

question_text: What does the idiom 'To beat around the bush' mean?

question_text: Select the meaning of: 'Bite the bullet'

question_text: What does the idiom 'At the drop of a hat' mean?

question_text: Select the meaning of: 'Spill the beans'

question_text: Select the meaning of: 'A piece of cake'

question_text: Select the one-word substitute for: 'A life history of a person written by himself'

question_text: Government by the people, of the people, and for the people:

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the option that will improve the underlined segment:
'He *has been working* here since five years.'
explanation: 'Five years' is a duration/period of time, which requires the preposition 'for' instead of 'since'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the improvement:
'The train *had left* before I reached the station.'
explanation: When two past actions occur, the earlier completed action takes Past Perfect ('had left') and the later action takes Simple Past ('reached'). Correct as is.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Improve the bracketed segment:
'She is senior [than me] in service.'
explanation: Latin comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' (senior, junior, prior, superior) take the preposition 'to', not 'than'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the improvement:
'He told me that he [does not like] classical music.'
explanation: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb ('told'), the reported clause shifts to past tense ('did not like').
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Improve the segment:
'Hardly had he arrived [when] the phone rang.'
explanation: 'Hardly' and 'Scarcely' are correlatively followed by 'when'. The sentence is grammatically correct as is.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the improvement:
'He is one of the tallest [boy] in the school.'
explanation: The phrase 'one of the' must be followed by a plural noun ('boys').
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Improve the underlined phrase:
'I *look forward to see* you soon.'
explanation: In the idiom 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition and must be followed by a gerund ('seeing').
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the improvement:
'If you *will work* hard, you will succeed.'
explanation: In future conditional clauses starting with 'if', the Simple Present tense ('work') is used, not 'will'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Improve the bracketed part:
'She sings [very well], doesn't she?'
explanation: For an affirmative statement in Simple Present with third person singular, the correct tag question is 'doesn't she?'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the improvement:
'He was accused [for] murder.'
explanation: The verb 'accuse' takes the fixed preposition 'of' ('accused of murder').
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the correct passive form of:
'The chef prepared a delicious dinner.'
option_a: A delicious dinner had been prepared by the chef.
option_b: A delicious dinner is prepared by the chef.
option_c: A delicious dinner was prepared by the chef.
option_d: A delicious dinner was being prepared by the chef.
explanation: Simple past active (prepared) transforms to was/were + V3 (was prepared).
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the active voice:
'The letter was delivered by the postman.'
option_a: The postman was delivering the letter.
option_c: The postman has delivered the letter.
explanation: Past passive 'was delivered' transforms into simple past active 'delivered'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert into passive voice:
'Open the door.'
explanation: Imperative commands transform into passive using 'Let + Object + be + V3'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Choose the passive voice:
'Who wrote this poem?'
option_b: By whom was this poem written?
option_c: By who was this poem written?
option_d: By whom this poem was written?
explanation: 'Who' changes to 'By whom'. Past tense question becomes 'By whom was this poem written?'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert into passive voice:
'They are building a new bridge over the river.'
option_a: A new bridge has been built over the river.
option_b: A new bridge was being built over the river.
option_c: A new bridge is being built over the river by them.
option_d: A new bridge is built over the river.
explanation: Present continuous active (are building) transforms to is/are + being + V3 (is being built).
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert to active voice:
'The project has been completed by the team.'
option_a: The team is completing the project.
option_c: The team had completed the project.
option_d: The team has completed the project.
explanation: Present perfect passive 'has been completed' converts to active 'has completed'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the passive form:
'Someone has stolen my watch.'
explanation: Present perfect passive of 'has stolen' is 'has been stolen' with indefinite agent 'someone' omitted.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert into passive voice:
'She will sing a patriotic song.'
option_a: A patriotic song would be sung by her.
option_b: A patriotic song will be sung by her.
option_c: A patriotic song is sung by her.
option_d: A patriotic song will sing by her.
explanation: Simple future active (will + V1) converts to 'will be + V3' (will be sung).
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert to active voice:
'Can this problem be solved by you?'
option_d: Can you be solving this problem?
explanation: Modal passive 'Can be solved' converts to active 'Can you solve'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert into passive voice:
'People speak English all over the world.'
option_a: English is being spoken all over the world.
option_b: English was spoken all over the world.
option_c: English has been spoken all over the world.
option_d: English is spoken all over the world.
explanation: Simple present active (speak) transforms to is + V3 (is spoken). General agent 'people' is omitted.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the correct indirect speech:
He said to me, 'I am reading a novel.'
option_a: He told me that he was reading a novel.
option_b: He told me that he is reading a novel.
option_c: He said me that he was reading a novel.
option_d: He told to me that he read a novel.
explanation: 'said to me' becomes 'told me'; Present Continuous 'am reading' becomes Past Continuous 'was reading'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert to indirect speech:
She said, 'Where are you going?'
option_a: She asked where was I going.
option_b: She asked where I was going.
option_c: She told where I was going.
option_d: She asked that where I was going.
explanation: Interrogative wh-questions do not use 'that'; word order becomes assertive: 'where I was going'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the indirect form:
The teacher said to the boys, 'Work hard.'
option_a: The teacher asked that boys should work hard.
option_b: The teacher said the boys to work hard.
option_c: The teacher advised the boys to work hard.
option_d: The teacher told the boys for working hard.
explanation: Imperative sentences transform with reporting verb 'advised/ordered' + object + infinitive 'to work'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert to indirect speech:
He said, 'The sun rises in the east.'
option_a: He told that the sun rises in the east.
option_b: He said that the sun rose in the east.
option_c: He said that the sun had risen in the east.
option_d: He said that the sun rises in the east.
explanation: Universal truths and scientific facts do not change tense in indirect speech.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the correct indirect form:
Rahul said, 'I have bought a new bicycle.'
option_a: Rahul said that he had bought a new bicycle.
option_b: Rahul said that he has bought a new bicycle.
option_c: Rahul said that he bought a new bicycle.
option_d: Rahul told that he had bought a new bicycle.
explanation: Present Perfect 'have bought' converts to Past Perfect 'had bought' with past reporting verb.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert to indirect speech:
Father said to his son, 'Do not waste your time.'
option_a: Father told his son do not waste your time.
option_b: Father forbade his son to waste his time.
option_c: Father asked his son to not waste time.
option_d: Father advised his son not waste his time.
explanation: 'forbade' incorporates negative meaning and takes positive infinitive 'to waste his time'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the indirect form:
She said, 'Alas! I have lost my purse.'
option_a: She said that alas she had lost her purse.
option_b: She exclaimed with joy that she lost her purse.
option_c: She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
option_d: She told that her purse was lost.
explanation: Exclamation of grief 'Alas!' converts to 'exclaimed with sorrow' and 'have lost' becomes 'had lost'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert to direct speech:
He asked me if I knew swimming.
option_b: He said to me, 'Did you know swimming?'
option_c: He asked to me, 'You know swimming?'
option_d: He said to me, 'Do you know swimming?'
explanation: Indirect 'asked if I knew' reverts to direct question in simple present: 'Do you know swimming?'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Select the indirect form:
Rohan said, 'I will visit Mumbai tomorrow.'
option_a: Rohan said that he would visit Mumbai the next day.
option_b: Rohan said that he will visit Mumbai tomorrow.
option_c: Rohan said that he would visit Mumbai tomorrow.
option_d: Rohan told that he will visit Mumbai the next day.
explanation: 'will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank

subject: English Language and Comprehension
question_text:
Convert to indirect speech:
The doctor said to the patient, 'Take these medicines regularly.'
option_a: The doctor ordered the patient take these medicines regularly.
option_b: The doctor advised the patient to take those medicines regularly.
option_c: The doctor said the patient to take those medicines.
option_d: The doctor asked the patient that he should take medicines.
explanation: 'these' becomes 'those'; reporting verb becomes 'advised' with 'to take'.
source_name: Staff Selection Commission Official Question Bank
